tasks.title: Docs: make Japanese validation-report follow-up handoff reproducible
tasks.outcome: A support or maintainer receiver can continue a Japanese follow-up from a path-free handoff without rewriting evidence, duplicating artifacts, or accepting a note.
non_goals: change the issue template, review ledger, support or verification implementation, or acceptance rules
change the Docker image, source helper, package-manager support, release identity, route chooser, or recovery implementation
ask for a private bag, map, or raw log upload
acceptance: The Japanese guide maps NOTE ONLY, SUPPORT REQUESTED, RETRY STARTED, NEW PAIR PREPARED, and STOPPED to a support, maintainer-review, or stop handoff with an explicit public status.

The handoff block records the disposition, action result, target, status, owner role, next review, and sanitized Details and Next without private paths; it does not grant acceptance or receipt-edit authority.
The guide keeps the original report, receipt, and hash immutable, permits one report/receipt pair per run, and forbids duplicate issue or session artifacts.
The card preserves one handoff per action audit, one evidence pair per run, and routes missing or mismatched identity/session/output back to STOP and safe support/retry.
The card preserves the v0.9.0 Docker versus v0.9.1 source-candidate identity boundary and tells the reader to stop when identity or session data is missing.
The existing support, session, privacy, independent-validation, and review-status guidance remains intact.
The documentation change needs no rosbag, hardware, network, or private log.

tasks.title: Docs: distinguish live and loop-optimized pose outputs
tasks.outcome: A user can select the intended live or loop-optimized pose topic, verify its frame, and avoid treating backend corrections as rewritten frontend odometry.
non_goals: change publishers, topic names, message types, or the feedback path
diagnose an individual bag or tune loop-closure parameters
claim that backend optimization repairs live frontend odometry
acceptance: The card identifies current_pose and path as live classic-frontend outputs and modified_path as the backend's optimized trajectory output.
The message types and header frames are checked with copy-ready ros2 topic commands before any viewer change.
The text explains that loop optimization may revise earlier trajectory estimates without rewriting already published live poses.
A reader can choose the matching RViz topic and fixed frame without guessing a transform.
The card separates a topic-selection problem from mapping drift or failed loop validation.
No accuracy, correction-feedback, or bag-specific success claim is added.

tasks.title: Docs: separate mapping, loop closure, and relocalization support
tasks.outcome: A user can distinguish continued map building, pose-graph loop optimization, localization against a prior map, and recovery after lost tracking before selecting a workflow.
non_goals: implement localization, relocalization, map continuation, or loop-closure feedback
turn experimental MID-360 evidence into a general support claim
prescribe bag-specific thresholds or algorithm changes
acceptance: The card defines mapping, backend loop closure, prior-map localization, and kidnap recovery as separate capabilities.
It states that loading or saving a PCD does not by itself create a supported prior-map localization workflow.
It explains that public mapping defaults keep automatic kidnap relocalization off and route a lost track or long scan gap to stop, split, review, and explicit map handling.
Experimental continuous MID-360 relocalization evidence is linked as bounded research evidence rather than advertised as general support.
Each user intent ends at the corresponding documented workflow or an explicit unsupported boundary.
No implementation, accuracy, or silent recovery promise is added.

tasks.title: Docs: add the classic-path IMU readiness card
tasks.outcome: A classic scanmatcher user can verify the IMU topic, frame, timing, measured extrinsic, and LiDAR scan period before enabling IMU prediction.
non_goals: add an IMU driver, calibration routine, or synchronization layer
change RKO-LIO or graph-backend IMU behavior
copy another robot's transform, scan period, or tuning values
acceptance: The card is explicitly scoped to classic scanmatcher use_imu and keeps the RKO-LIO input contract separate.
Copy-ready checks verify sensor_msgs/msg/Imu, a non-empty header.frame_id, advancing timestamps, and a positive observed rate.
The directed base-to-IMU TF is checked and an unknown or guessed extrinsic stops the procedure.
The card explains that scan_period is the LiDAR scan duration, not the IMU publication period, and requires a measured or specified value.
A bounded launch/YAML example shows imu_topic, use_imu, scan_period, and the measured frame relationship without adding a vendor preset.
Readiness for one controlled run is kept separate from accuracy or hardware support.

tasks.title: Docs: triage a long-route mapping stop without inventing a distance limit
tasks.outcome: A user can separate stopped input, a dead node, registration refusal, compute backlog, storage exhaustion, and viewer-only symptoms before assuming a maximum mapping distance.
non_goals: claim a universal maximum distance, runtime, memory footprint, or accuracy
tune an individual bag, sensor, route, or compute platform
change runtime limits, voxel sizes, queue depths, or failure handling
request a private bag, map, or location-bearing raw log
acceptance: The card states that route length alone is not a supported universal limit and points to bounded public benchmark evidence instead of inventing one.
Copy-ready checks distinguish whether the input topic advances, the mapping nodes are alive, warnings or refusals occurred, storage remains available, and the viewer is following the intended output.
Each symptom ends in one safe next action: preserve the retained session, stop the run, repair the named input/resource/failure condition, and rerun a bounded control.
VoxelGrid refusal remains a fail-closed diagnostic and is not answered by blindly lowering or increasing a leaf size.
The card separates process survival and map publication from validated map quality or accuracy.
The support handoff remains sanitized and does not ask for private geometry or location-bearing artifacts.
